items.note: Fixes h, v, N, m and I, gives both scalar constructions and the eight-row schedule, derives the net change (JV+RG)x independent of scratch, the bit and complex coefficient checks, the three-stage chain (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x), and the wire counts W_b, W_c, all as in lines 741-783. The head step S2.1 loosely calls all three stages forward invocations, but S2.1.7 states the inverse stage correctly.

States frames D_v shared at a gate, edge change D_vD_u^{-1}, the implemented operator D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} and the route operator eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}. Derives it by the paper's invariant: logical array defined as D_in^{-1}f, edges change frames, and R-linearity makes the common frame commute with the pointwise gate.

Gives the two bilinear forms with <t_S,t_T>=|S cap T|-1, the terminal labels, the interstage transitions, the eight gate labels, the full residual table (dimensions match lines 1022-1043), the confinement of decreases to centre 3->4, telescoping to Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich, the binary orthonormal bases and L/N=100/539, 101/539. S2.3.3.6 simplifies the nonalternating argument slightly (see errors).

Assigns P_U at gates and sinks and -P_{U_a} at X_a sources, proves rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, adds the N rank-one source edges 2P_{U_a}, gets s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b with deficit N-2L_b, and the endpoint identity I_m; S2.7.2 uses the frames Phi_M to get the shear H<-H+D on every role, as in lines 1156-1172 and 1504-1533.

States the phase frames C_U, one kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector, s_c=W_cm-2N+2L_c<W_cm and C^{otimes m} on every role (also on k columns). Derives it through weight additivity mod 4, odd weights, the H diag(1,-1) H = X conversion, the X_a->Y_a pair with weight 27 and the Z corrections, matching lines 1231-1315.

Has L<N/2, both strict savings s<Wm with their deficits, the exact eta_b=339/22587335000000 and eta_c=73/19906842167500, the bound eta>20*2^{-50}, log m<20 and the exponential inequality giving s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, as at lines 1319-1346.

S1.1 lists the four elementary operations with O(V) cost. S1.2 gives the controlled-shift mechanism (split each fibre at Q-a, merge in the opposite order) from lines 575-590, but the claim drops the prime radix and coprime denominators and leaves the b^{O(1)} offset condition to the quote. The proofs of the elementary operations (q^2-way splits, row classes) and of unit multiplication are not shown.

Gives A=E_1 Pi E_2 by the paper's topmost-row, rightmost-pivot elimination, triangular transforms by controlled shifts in descending order with a fixed odd prime, the conjugation E_2, E_1^{-1}, and the three-step realisation of H_i<-H_i+D_j with one interchange, so exactly a interchanges plus O(V).

Follows the proof: m fields of b=e/m digits, cyclic row split into W streams of volume V/W, Phi_M frames giving Phi_{I_m}, the three-step interchange, s recursive calls, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), the geometric-sum case split, F_k=O(e^tau), and the fixed-tape stack schedule and descriptor accounting.

Reproduces k, rho, the four field orders, the row field R=q^{2rho}>=W^k padded to R'<2R, the base-m pieces with cost O(V) sum a_j m^{j tau}=O(Ve^tau), the padding from [2^u] to [q^e], and the unequal-width bit move.

Gives the C identities, P_M X_v P_M^{-1}=X_{Mv}, the coordinate form of the edge identity, the slot/column layout with one child per residual direction, the inverse-child identity, at most m(m-1)+3m row additions, exactly s_c children on e/m axes, and H_0^{otimes D}=b^D S_D C^{otimes D} S_D.

Covers the eight conditional updates and their parity cycles, the packed cyclic shifts, the guard interval 10<=g<=2^{K-1}-11, delta_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}}, T_0S_0^{-1} permuting B, swaps plus O(V) rotations, extraction and radix-sort repair, the three cost terms and their o(1) normalisation, and the application to a change of basis at O(V((eK)^tau+1)). The head step omits the A_rect=O(p) condition, which is minor.

Gives the individual-kernel cost O(Ve), s calls per node with overhead O(V((eK)^tau+1)), q_0 and k_0 with row padding to W^{k_0}, volume V/W per role, F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) with leaves O(e), the bounds O(e^lambda) and O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}), and the base-m sum to O(d^{lambda'}), as in lines 2286-2448.

States the layer H=H_0^{otimes D} on D<=d chunks of K=floor(d^c) bits, returned as Q_p(Hz) in O(Vd^{lambda'}) with error <sqrt2 2^{-p}. Derives the guard width Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1})=o(p) from E, B, nu=11 and A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E, and the final truncation from absolute row sum one. The per-call uniformity check of lines 2696-2735 is only covered through S2.9.2.10.

Covers character cancellation without division (no two-torsion), decimation in frequency, bit-reversed storage B_t and the opposite procedure F_t^+B_t^{-1}, grouped rounds with J_E, the layout L (prefix moves O(dK), Dq-1 chunk exchanges O(Tp pK^{tau-1})), layer calls per round, J_E Q_p=Q_p J_E and the sqrt2 ell 2^{-p} error. S3.3's head claim that every round is a layer call is loose (see errors).

Follows the proof: B_0=2^{4p}, signed evaluation with carries in {-1,0}, four products by the established multiplier, centred extraction with carries in {0,1} using |h_j|<B_0/2, negacyclic wrap and truncation, cost O(rp log(rp)).

States M_r(f,g)=(f*g)/T with error sqrt2 M(3ell+1)2^{-p} and the stated cost. Derives it by the normalisation identity, P(LBu,LBv)=LB P(u,v), and the 2delta, +eta, +delta error chain scaled by M, as in lines 3414-3495.

Gives S, T, the identity TP_sF_s=P_tF_t S, the Neumann inverse of N=CTD, the normalisations multiplying to 2^{-2alpha^2}, A and B_0 as contractions, the quoted error and time table, the ordered selection C, and the tensor form with linewise error dp^2, time O(dTp^{3/2+delta}alpha) and axis exposure O(Tpd^2(1+ell^tau)).

States the chirp identity and the cancellation (RF^+_s)[(RF_s u)(RF_s v)]=(u*v)/S^2. Derives them by the coefficient check, F_q^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F_q^+ with t_i a unit mod s_i, commuting permutations with pointwise products, and the two normalisations, exactly as in lines 3938-3988.

Gives all fixed exponents and their compatibility inequalities, the sizes b, p, d, K, T, r, t_i with their Theta-bounds and comparison constants, alpha, gamma, eta, the prime-interval count giving distinct odd primes, T/2<S<T, alpha^4 theta_i>p, the n^{o(1)} prime search, and the no-wraparound and capacity bounds.

Gives Phi as an algebra isomorphism, the triangular formula b_i=a_i+mu_i sum_{j<i}a_jP_j, updates in order d,...,1, valid-interval rotations preserving zero padding, prefix-controlled cyclic shifts, and O(d^2) axis moves costing O(Tpd^2(1+ell^tau)).

Gives the twist x_d->zeta y, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j, M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+f, iota D_+g)=(f*g)/T, the computed sequence f', g', h' and its cost. S6.2 supplies the three twist errors of 4 each.

Composes A, the chirp transform and B_0 with the 2^gamma scale into the source transform with exact counterpart RF_s and its conjugate, then lists the six steps (digits scaled 2^{-b-2}, Phi, two transforms, pointwise product, opposite transform with S, scale 2^{2b+4}S, rounding, Phi^{-1}, carries) and why the two occurrences of S undo different normalisations.

Chains E_ring<5TL, 6TL, 8TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL, 2E_s+2, 3E_s+2 and E_w<28*2^gamma T^2L with disk margins, then the final bound 448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2 using gamma<=b/4, rounding, and the carry invariant, matching lines 4546-4806.

Reproduces the cost table and its powers, the seven margins with min g_2=2^{-181}=2kappa, the derivation of each row, setup and exceptional sorting as o(V), log-power absorption and the schoolbook cutoff, giving O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}).

S0 says the bound disproves the n log n optimality conjecture in this model, but never states what the negation requires (one machine with liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n)=0) or that the power saving gives limit zero.

errors.says: Three stages of forward invocations y_S -> y_S+x_S send (X_a,Y_a) -> (-Y_a,X_a).
errors.paper: Stage 2 runs the inverse forward schedule with logical source Y and target X, effecting X <- X-Y. Only stages 1 and 3 are forward invocations from X to Y. The plan's own S2.1.7 states this correctly.

errors.says: Over F_2 every nonzero residual is nonalternating because it contains a norm-one coordinate vector outside the supports of the earlier tensor vectors.
errors.paper: Coordinate units are chosen only inside B, Q^perp, triple complements and full spaces. The lines P and Q contribute their own norm-one vectors (triple-indicator tensors, not coordinate vectors), and a norm-one vector of each tensor summand is the tensor product of these choices. So a residual such as P tensor t^perp need not contain a coordinate vector.

errors.says: The layout L lets each round of the multidimensional transform be one simultaneous butterfly layer.
errors.paper: Only the rounds on the remaining K-bit chunks call the simultaneous layer. The leading long-axis round and the at most b+1<=K rounds on prefix slots process their bits individually at O(Tp) each, giving the O(TpdK) term. The plan's own S3.3.6 states this.

chain: The tree reaches O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}) by the paper's route. It builds the scalar exchange networks, puts frames on them, attaches labels and counts ranks to get s<Wm and tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, then derives the interchange recurrence and the butterfly-layer recurrence and feeds them into the synthetic transforms. Gaussian resampling, the chirp with permutation cancellation, the CRT map and the twist complete the source transform, followed by the six-step algorithm, the exact-recovery error chain and the margin table. The coverage only thins at the base: the elementary stream operations are stated rather than proved, and the Gaussian facts are quoted from Harvey and van der Hoeven, as in the paper. No link in the chain is missing.

steps.note: S2.1.0 fixes h=100, v=binom(h,3), N=v^3, m=h^3 and the banks X_a,Y_a indexed by a in T^3. S2.1 and S2.1.7 give the fixed linear network sending (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) and restoring every scratch wire.
One invertible frame is shared at each gate and commutes with the pointwise gate by R-linearity. The network implements D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, so each edge costs only the change D_vD_u^{-1}.

Gates and terminals get nondegenerate subspaces of F^{otimes3} of dimension m, and every edge joins nested labels. The only decreasing edges are the central wires from time 3 to time 4, each losing P tensor F of dimension h.
S2.3.5.2 gives rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U for nested labels. S2.3.5.3 names the N source edges 2P_{U_a} of rank one as the only exceptions.
S2.3.3.5 derives sum |Delta dim|=Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich from source and sink dimension sums and telescoping. S2.3.5.1 gives s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b.
S2.3.4 gives L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2. The deficits N-2L_b>0 and 2N-2L_c>0 give s<Wm.
Endpoint difference P_{U_a^perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m on X_a, zero to identity on the other roles. With frames Phi_M this gives the shear H<-H+D on every role (S2.7.2).
A rank-a matrix factors as E_1 Pi E_2, and the shear costs exactly a interchanges plus O(V). Each interchange is a recursive call, so a node makes s calls in all (S2.7.4).
Children have volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), and s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50} from eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20. The geometric sum gives F_k=O(e^tau).

central.summary: All nine steps are reconstructed with their defining quantities and in the order the paper uses them: the fixed h=100 exchange network, frames, nested labels with the h-loss on central 3->4 edges, rank equal to dimension change plus N source ranks, the budget Wm-N+2L, L/N=100/539<1/2, the endpoint identity giving the shear, rank-many interchanges per edge, and the recurrence with tau=1-2^{-50}.
